candidates.label: Antakya (ancient Antioch on the Orontes)
candidates.support: Antakya is the accepted continuation of the Hellenistic and Roman city, founded around 300 BC by Seleucus I Nicator and renamed Theoupolis in the Byzantine period. Pleiades' representative point for the ancient city sits about two kilometers from Wikidata's point, a normal spread for a city of this size given its position across the Orontes floodplain.

summary.text: Antioch on the Orontes was a major Hellenistic and Roman city in northern Syria, standing on the river's left bank about 15 miles from the Mediterranean, with its port at Seleucia. Founded in 301 BC by Seleucus I Nicator, a king who had just become master of Syria, it grew by Paul's day into the third city of the Roman world after Rome and Alexandria, and the capital of the Roman province of Syria. Seleucus had settled Jews in the city with equal rights to its Greek citizens, and a few decades before Paul's time, Herod the Great paved the city's twenty-furlong main street with polished marble and lined it with covered colonnades on both sides, a street that the Jewish historian Josephus says had before been "shunned by all men... because it was full of dirt and filthiness."

history.text: Acts reports that believers scattered by persecution first brought the gospel to Antioch, and that the Jerusalem church sent Barnabas there; he in turn brought Saul from Tarsus, and the two taught there for a year, during which "the disciples were first called Christians." Acts also says that the Holy Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul in Antioch for the missionary journey the church sent them on, and the city hosted a dispute over keeping the Jewish law that the apostles in Jerusalem settled by letter. Paul also recalled opposing the apostle Peter "to his face" in Antioch, because, in Paul's words, Peter "stood condemned."

The church at Antioch became known as the mother church of Gentile Christianity, a reputation it long kept. The city suffered repeatedly from earthquakes, and it lost its place as the leading city of Syria only after the Arab conquest restored that status to Damascus.
Today the site survives as Antakya, a city in southern Türkiye on the Orontes river.

scripture.textWEB: These words pleased the whole multitude. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch,
They therefore who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.
But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.
The report concerning them came to the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem. They sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch,
When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
Now in these days, prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
As any of the disciples had plenty, each determined to send relief to the brothers who lived in Judea;
Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.” Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
When they had arrived and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised after the custom of Moses, you can’t be saved.”

Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole assembly, to choose men out of their company, and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers.
They wrote these things by their hand: “The apostles, the elders, and the brothers, to the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.
So, when they were sent off, they came to Antioch. Having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.
Having spent some time there, he departed and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
But when Peter came to Antioch, I resisted him to his face, because he stood condemned.
Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.
